name: Job tiering BackgroundTasks arq Taskiq Celery Temporal
short_definition: Choose background execution by durability and orchestration needs: FastAPI BackgroundTasks for request-scoped best-effort work; Redis/AMQP task queues (Taskiq preferred greenfield async, arq acceptable but maintenance-only, Celery for mature sync ecosystems) for durable independent jobs; Temporal for multi-step durable workflows, sagas, and long-running agents — not as a first queue for simple email sends.
scope_in: Four-tier job selection; FastAPI BackgroundTasks semantics and caveats; Taskiq/arq/Celery feature fit; Temporal when to graduate; broker choice (Redis/RabbitMQ); worker deploy model; enqueue-from-API patterns; scheduling delays; result backends; observability of queues; CPU vs I/O worker pools.
scope_out: Idempotency/DLQ deep patterns (py-idempotency-retries); full Temporal agent design (py-durable-workflows); asyncio task groups for in-request concurrency (py-async-model); cron-only ops without a queue (py-cli-scripts).
defaults: Tier 0 — BackgroundTasks: after-response hooks that may be lost on process crash (metrics flush, tiny non-critical side effects). Max seconds; no retries guarantee; same process as API. Tier 1 — Async queue (Taskiq + Redis or RabbitMQ): default for FastAPI/async services needing durable jobs, retries, independent scale (emails, webhooks outbound, LLM calls, report gen). Prefer Taskiq over arq for new greenfield (arq is maintenance-only as of 2026). Tier 2 — Celery: adopt when org already standardized on Celery/Flower, need vast broker/ops ecosystem, or sync-heavy Django-era workers — not default for new async-first apps. Tier 3 — Temporal: multi-step business processes, human waits, compensations, durable agent loops spanning minutes–days. Always separate worker processes from API for Tier≥1. Enqueue with job type + versioned payload; never pass open DB sessions into jobs.
decision_gates: USE BackgroundTasks when: work is short, loss-tolerant, and tied to request lifecycle (or explicitly documented best-effort). USE Taskiq/arq when: must survive API restart, need retries/backoff, scale workers separately, I/O-bound async. USE Celery when: existing Celery ops expertise, need max ecosystem (Flower, battle-tested routing), sync libraries dominate. USE Temporal when: workflow state machine, saga, long sleep/wait, exactly-once process orchestration beyond a single task function. DO NOT use BackgroundTasks for payments, billing, or anything requiring ack. DO NOT use Temporal for 'send welcome email' alone. DO NOT run heavy jobs on the API event loop without a queue.
do_dont: DO: define job payloads as Pydantic models; include correlation/request_id; set timeouts; separate queues by priority/SLA; graceful worker shutdown; health checks on workers; version task names. DON'T: store huge blobs in Redis job args (use object storage refs); share AsyncSession across process boundary; fire Celery task for every log line; block async worker with CPU without process pool; rely on BackgroundTasks for webhook delivery guarantees; ignore broker disk/memory limits.
code_skeleton:
# --- Tier 0: BackgroundTasks ---
from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

def write_audit(user_id: str) -> None:
    # best-effort; may be lost if process dies
    ...

@app.post('/signup')
async def signup(bg: BackgroundTasks):
    bg.add_task(write_audit, 'u1')
    return {'ok': True}

# --- Tier 1: Taskiq (preferred async queue) ---
# uv add taskiq taskiq-redis
from taskiq_redis import RedisStreamBroker, RedisAsyncResultBackend

result_backend = RedisAsyncResultBackend(redis_url='redis://localhost:6379')
broker = RedisStreamBroker(url='redis://localhost:6379').with_result_backend(result_backend)

@broker.task(retry_on_error=True)
async def send_email(user_id: str, template: str) -> None:
    ...

# API: await send_email.kiq(user_id, 'welcome')
# Worker: taskiq worker app.broker:broker

# --- Tier 1b: arq (maintenance-only; existing code ok) ---
# async def send_email(ctx, user_id: str): ...
# class WorkerSettings:
#     functions = [send_email]
#     redis_settings = RedisSettings(host='localhost')

# --- Tier 2: Celery sketch ---
# from celery import Celery
# celery_app = Celery('jobs', broker='redis://localhost:6379/0')
# @celery_app.task(bind=True, max_retries=5)
# def send_email(self, user_id: str): ...

# --- Tier 3: Temporal (workflow + activities) ---
# @workflow.defn
# class OnboardUser:
#     @workflow.run
#     async def run(self, user_id: str) -> None:
#         await workflow.execute_activity(send_email, user_id, start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
failure_modes: 1) BackgroundTasks lost on deploy mid-flight. 2) Redis as broker without persistence → job loss. 3) Unbounded queue growth under worker outage. 4) Prefetch/ack-too-early causing at-most-once surprises (Celery defaults). 5) Worker OOM from large payloads. 6) Dual execution without idempotency. 7) API and worker dependency skew (different code versions). 8) ETA/countdown jobs held in memory forever. 9) Blocking the asyncio loop in Taskiq/arq workers. 10) Using Temporal as a dumb queue and paying complexity tax.
anti_patterns: BackgroundTasks for payment capture; Celery always by default in async FastAPI greenfield; arq for new systems without noting maintenance-only; one mega-queue for all priorities; pickle of arbitrary Python objects from untrusted sources; running workers as threads inside uvicorn without isolation; sleeping in workflows instead of Temporal timers when durability needed; enqueueing from request without rate limits.
tools: Tier0: FastAPI/Starlette BackgroundTasks. Tier1: Taskiq (+ taskiq-redis, taskiq-aio-pika, taskiq-fastapi); arq (legacy/maint); alternatives Dramatiq, RQ, Procrastinate/PgQueuer (Postgres-backed). Tier2: Celery + Redis/RabbitMQ + Flower. Tier3: Temporal SDK (Python). Ops: Redis/RabbitMQ metrics, OTel, structured logs. Scheduler: broker delays, Taskiq scheduler, or Temporal timers — not API process crons for critical work.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: Taskiq ~0.12.4 (May 2026); taskiq-redis active (2026); taskiq-fastapi 0.5.x; arq 0.28.0 (Apr 2026) labeled maintenance-only; Celery 5.6.x in 2026 comparisons; FastAPI BackgroundTasks per current FastAPI docs (caveat points to Celery-class tools for heavy work). Temporal Python SDK current stable — pin in lockfile when used. Prefer Taskiq or Celery over new arq adoptions.

deprecation_watch: New arq greenfield (maintenance-only mode); Celery as mandatory default for all FastAPI apps; Huey for large multi-service (fine for tiny apps only); storing job state only in memory; APScheduler inside API container as sole production scheduler for critical jobs; pickle serializers for multi-language or untrusted payloads.
ts_boundary: Next BFF enqueues via Python HTTP/internal API or shared Redis only with strict contracts — prefer calling Python 'enqueue' endpoint over writing queue messages from TS (avoids dual schema). Return job_id to UI for polling if needed. Do not run long LLM work on Vercel serverless without an external worker.
rust_boundary: CPU-heavy or ultra-high-throughput consumers may be Rust workers on the same broker (Redis streams/NATS). Keep payload schema versioned (JSON). Temporal activities can be multi-language. Prefer Python for AI/LLM orchestration workers unless latency profile forces Rust.
supabase_boundary: Jobs that write DB must use server credentials and idempotent upserts. Do not hold Supabase realtime as a job queue. Outbox table in Postgres can pair with workers for reliable publish. RLS: workers typically service_role — enforce tenant checks in job code.
boundary_contracts: Job payload JSON schema/version field; OpenAPI for enqueue endpoints; env REDIS_URL/BROKER_URL/TEMPORAL_HOST; MCP tools that enqueue must timeout and auth. Document tier per job type in code (decorator or registry).
decision_matrix_row: Problem: best-effort after response → BackgroundTasks. Problem: durable async job FastAPI greenfield → Taskiq (+Redis/Rabbit). Problem: existing Celery platform → Celery. Problem: multi-step durable process/agent → Temporal. Problem: simple Postgres-only shop → Procrastinate/PgQueuer optional. Problem: in-request parallel I/O → anyio task groups not a job queue.
threats: Poison payloads causing worker RCE via unsafe deserialize; unauthenticated enqueue endpoints; job data PII in Redis without TTL/encryption; privilege escalation if workers have broader secrets than API; DoS by flooding queues; SSRF from jobs fetching user URLs.
mitigations: JSON serializers only; auth on enqueue; least-privilege worker secrets; payload size limits; queue rate limits; network egress controls for workers; no pickle; scrub PII from job args where possible; separate queues for untrusted vs trusted work.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: pick tier explicitly; Taskiq (not arq) for new async queues; separate worker process for durable work; Pydantic payloads; timeouts; never BackgroundTasks for money/compliance. MUST NOT: pickle; pass Session into jobs; Celery-by-default in async greenfield without reason; Temporal for single fire-and-forget email; unbounded retries without DLQ plan (see py-idempotency-retries).
tests_required: Unit test task pure functions; broker integration optional with testcontainers Redis; assert BackgroundTasks invoked in ASGI tests only for tier0; contract tests for payload schema; load smoke for enqueue path; Temporal workflow unit tests when used.
ci_gates: pytest; import-linter or grep ban pickle on job modules; docker-compose worker boots; version pin audit; no secrets in job fixtures.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: taskiq broker, WorkerSettings/arq only with note, celery app isolated, temporal workflow.defn, separate worker service, Pydantic job payloads, tier comments. NEGATIVE: BackgroundTasks for payments, pickle.loads job body, jobs using request-scoped Session, only API process no worker for durable tasks, new arq without maintenance caveat, Temporal for trivial single calls.
skill_module_bullets:
- Job tiers: BackgroundTasks → Taskiq/arq queue → Celery (legacy/ecosystem) → Temporal (durable workflows).
- Greenfield async: Taskiq + Redis/Rabbit; arq is maintenance-only.
- BackgroundTasks are best-effort, same-process — not for critical side effects.
- Separate worker processes; versioned JSON payloads; no pickle.
- Temporal for multi-step/saga/agent durability — not a simple mailer.
- Enqueue from API with job_id; scale workers independently.
- Cross-link idempotency/retries for at-least-once safety.
action_items: 1) Publish tier table in references/python.md (and future background-jobs.md). 2) Scan for BackgroundTasks on critical paths. 3) Prefer Taskiq scaffold in templates. 4) Note arq maintenance-only. 5) Link Temporal item py-durable-workflows.

conflicts_noted: Celery still wins on ecosystem size; async benches favor Taskiq/Dramatiq/Repid/FastStream — greenfield async FastAPI should not default Celery. arq still popular in blogs but officially maintenance-only — conflict between tutorials and project status. Temporal vs queues: category difference often blurred in marketing. Repid/FastStream strong 2026 contenders but less standard in this monorepo — Taskiq is the recommended middle path unless team chooses Celery/Temporal for clear reasons.
